articles.title: IAS officer, booked for abusing, attacking cops at Bengaluru pub, transferred
articles.description: Vikas Marmat, an IAS officer from Andhra Pradesh, has been transferred following an incident at a Bengaluru nightclub. This incident involved an inspection by the police to check for underage drinking. During the inspection, Marmat allegedly abused police officers after they requested age verification from women. He has been named the primary accused alongside three others who were also booked in the case.

articles.description: A viral video has raised safety concerns after three motorcycles skidded on Chingrighata flyover. Authorities are investigating whether the festive road beautification compromised safety due to inappropriate surface coatings. Experts highlight that poorly applied paint can reduce tyre grip, especially when wet conditions occur. Senior officials indicated that steps will be taken based on expert recommendations regarding road surface materials.

articles.title: NYC subway hides ventilation shaft and emergency exit behind 1847 Brooklyn townhouse façade
articles.description: Nestled at 58 Joralemon Street in Brooklyn Heights lies a historic brownstone that harbors a subway ventilation shaft beneath its surface. Established in 1847, it transformed into a vital transit hub in 1908 under the Brooklyn Rapid Transit Company. The building's unchanged facade allows it to integrate seamlessly into the neighborhood while fulfilling crucial safety roles.

articles.title: Lake Ringgold Reservoir Permit: Judge overturns state approval; Wichita Falls weighs appeal
articles.description: In a significant legal development, a Texas judge has scrapped the permit for the Lake Ringgold reservoir, amidst ongoing opposition from local ranchers concerned about environmental issues and property rights. Wichita Falls aims to appeal this ruling as they push for their water supply plans. This situation underscores the complex relationship between infrastructure advancements and conservation, with the city's next moves remaining unclear.

articles.title: Stock market today: BSE Sensex jumps 400 points, Nifty50 opens above 22,700
articles.full_text: BSE Sensex rallied 802.45 points, or 1.10%, to 73,584.34, even as several index constituents traded in the red. Among the top Sensex losers, Bharat Electronics (BEL) fell 0.88% to Rs 378.75, while Power Grid Corporation declined 0.50% to Rs 248.50. Trent dropped 0.39% to Rs 2,954, followed by Titan, which slipped 0.36% to Rs 4,428.95. State Bank of India (SBI) lost 0.35% to Rs 950.85, while Adani Ports declined 0.34% to Rs 1,739.10. NTPC was also marginally lower, falling 0.10% to Rs 313.70. Despite these losses among individual stocks, the benchmark index advanced 1.10%. Among the top gainers, Tech Mahindra led the pack, rising 2.13% to Rs 1,609.60, followed by TCS, which gained 2.08% to Rs 2,349.85. Infosys advanced 1.56% to Rs 1,105.85, while ICICI Bank climbed 1.27% to Rs 1,356.25. Bharti Airtel and HCLTech rose 0.65% and 0.63% to Rs 1,810.70 and Rs 1,337.40, respectively. ITC gained 0.59% to Rs 262.80, while Axis Bank rose 0.56% to Rs 1,272.25. HDFC Bank was up 0.47% at Rs 714.05, Hindustan Unilever gained 0.45% to Rs 1,905.50, and Asian Paints advanced 0.43% to Rs 2,359.15. UltraTech Cement rose 0.36% to Rs 10,785, while M&M and Reliance Industries edged up 0.21% and 0.17% to Rs 2,805 and Rs 1,178, respectively. Tata Steel gained 0.14% to Rs 174.55, while IndiGo traded unchanged at Rs 4,723.80. Stock market today: Check stock recommendations for October 15, 2026 Dalal Street is expected to open lower on Thursday, tracking weakness across Asian markets after a faster-than-expected rise in US consumer price inflation strengthened expectations of another Federal Reserve rate hike this year. Higher US interest rates can make emerging markets such as India less attractive to overseas investors. Foreign investors had sold Indian equities for 14 consecutive sessions through Wednesday, taking year-to-date outflows to a record $32.7 billion. GIFT Nifty futures stood at 22,606.5, indicating a negative start for the Nifty50, which had settled at 22,622.70 in the previous session. Crude oil prices retreated in early trading, with Brent and US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures falling by more than $1 as investors assessed fresh threats to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the possibility of US sanctions relief for vessels carrying petroleum. Brent crude declined 1.30%, or $1.38, to $104.70 a barrel, while WTI fell 1.07%, shedding $1.02 to trade at $94.07. The pullback followed a sharp rise in WTI during the previous session, when prices reached a three-week high. The earlier rally came after the Houthis attacked Saudi Aramco's headquarters and Iran announced new tactics targeting vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's stated aim was to keep oil prices high. The latest price movement reflected investors weighing these shipping-related threats against the possibility of measures to reduce petroleum transport costs. Emerging Asian equities surrendered some of their gains during Wednesday's afternoon trading as investors assessed the sustainability of the artificial intelligence rally and growing competition from Chinese rivals to South Korean chipmakers. Regional semiconductor stocks struggled to recover following a global selloff in the sector. Investors also evaluated the impact of higher bond yields on substantial AI-related spending. Reports about technological advances by China's CXMT raised questions about South Korea's competitive position in memory chips. Against this backdrop, South Korea's KOSPI erased its early gains to end Wednesday 0.4% lower, extending its losing streak to six consecutive sessions. Samsung Electronics traded flat, while SK Hynix declined 1.7%. KOSPI had fallen around 35% from its record high in June. The regional weakness highlighted the pressure on Asian technology stocks as investors reassessed semiconductor valuations, competitive dynamics and the cost of AI-related investment. Rupee is expected to open higher, supported by a pullback in US treasury yields after an initial rise following sticky US inflation data. Traders are still pricing in limited chances of a Federal Reserve rate hike in October. The currency is expected to open in the 95.02-95.06 range against the US dollar, compared with its Wednesday close of 95.15. Attention remains focused on the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the extent of measures it would take to support rupee. Stock markets ended lower on Wednesday, with Sensex falling 251.89 points, or 0.34%, to 72,781.89, and the Nifty50 declining 99.25 points, or 0.44%, to 22,622.70. Profit-booking after the previous session's rally, rising wholesale inflation and firm crude oil prices weighed on sentiment. Markets are expected to open lower on Thursday, tracking weak Asian cues after higher-than-expected US inflation fuelled bets on another Federal Reserve rate hike. Foreign investors continued to sell Indian equities, with year-to-date outflows reaching $32.7 billion. Investors are also tracking oil prices amid concerns over Strait of Hormuz shipping, the rupee's movement and the RBI's support measures. Wipro's second-quarter results were another key focus.

articles.title: Five Indiana engineering students built a 12-hour wearable that helps visually impaired users detect obstacles beyond a cane or guide dog
articles.description: Rose-Hulman students have developed a remarkable wearable device tailored for visually impaired individuals. This innovative headgear employs advanced sensors to identify surrounding obstacles, providing users with haptic feedback. With a remarkable twelve-hour battery life on a single charge, this device empowers users with greater independence. The project's goal is to enhance the day-to-day experiences of those with vision impairments.

articles.title: Salman Khan says a biopic on his life will never be made
articles.description: Salman Khan has stated that he will never allow a biopic based on his life to be created. During an interview on 'Koffee With Karan', he mentioned that his life experiences remain private. Although he humorously named several filmmakers for hypothetical adaptations, he emphasized the fictional nature of such discussions. Salman also declined to write an autobiography, citing potential pain from reopening old wounds.
